topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by introducing the themes of immune recognition, inflammation initiation, and resolution.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how the innate immune system detects infections and tissue damage through conserved molecular patterns and germline-encoded receptors.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor families and signaling mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the major classes of pattern recognition receptors, their intracellular signaling pathways, and the assembly of inflammasomes that mature pro-inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Inflammatory signaling, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic consequences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how sentinel cells mediate local leukocyte extravasation, facilitate lymphatic priming of adaptive immunity, and risk triggering severe systemic pathologies like sepsis.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the passive and active mechanisms that extinguish inflammation, rebuild damaged tissues, and contain persistent infections through chronic granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding framing and introduces the subject of the next lecture.
